newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index down 0.5 pct at 328.79.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index down 0.5 pct at 328.79.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars, fell 0.5 percent to 328.79 by the start on Thursday.
Latin America fell 1.2 percent day-on-day to 628.36, Asia was off 0.2 percent at 266.07 and Europe, Middle East and Africa were down 0.2 percent at 156.98.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was down 0.53 percent day-on-day at 178.09 at 1345 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 30 emerging market countries after adding Russia, Slovakia, Egypt and Morocco on February 3. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.15 percent to 127.17 by the start of trade on Thursday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was up 0.29 percent at 105.46, Asia fell 0.03 to 133.72 and East Europe was up 0.31 at 158.88.
